He was born in 1712 in Paris and died in 1785. Choiseul's diplomatic career was marked by his service as the French Foreign Minister from 1750 to 1754 and his role in negotiating the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle in 1748, which ended the War of the Austrian Succession. He also contributed to the development of the French East India Company and the French colonization of Canada. Choiseul's legacy is significant in the history of Prussia and the French monarchy, and he is remembered as a key figure in the rise of Prussia as a major European power. The Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle, which he negotiated, had a lasting impact on the balance of power in Europe and paved the way for the rise of Prussia as a dominant force. Choiseul's diplomatic efforts also helped to establish France as a major player in European politics and diplomacy. 

Choiseul's significance extends beyond his diplomatic career, as he was also a key figure in the development of the French Enlightenment, a philosophical and intellectual movement that emphasized reason, science, and progress. He was a strong advocate for the principles of the Enlightenment and worked to promote them throughout his career.

The legacy of César Gabriel de Choiseul can be seen in the many institutions and organizations he helped to establish, including the French East India Company and the French colonization of Canada. His diplomatic efforts also had a lasting impact on the balance of power in Europe and paved the way for the rise of Prussia as a dominant force. Choiseul's commitment to the principles of the Enlightenment and his role in promoting them throughout his career have made him a significant figure in the history of European politics and diplomacy.
